title: enforce-rbacv2-ttls-add-auditlink-hmac-and-kms-region-affinity-validator
author: Amina Patel
description: Motivation: several operational incidents exposed long-lived delegation grants and unverifiable audit links when operators replayed requests across regions. This change introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) an RBACv2 policy TTL enforcement layer that rejects or soft-expunges stale delegation bindings; 2) an audit-link HMAC signing scheme so downstream consumers can validate event continuity without exposing key material; and 3) a KMS region-affinity validator that checks KMS wrap/unwrap requests against the tenant's declared region pins and fails fast when mismatches are detected. The work here is intentionally conservative: enforcement is gated behind a feature flag and we ship a migration helper to identify bindings that would be impacted. Checklist: - [x] implement policy TTL validator with unit tests - [x] wire TTL checks into policy evaluation path (non-blocking mode behind flag) - [x] implement audit-link signing middleware and verification util - [x] implement KMS region-affinity validator and attach to crypto-proxy - [x] add migration script to identify stale bindings and generate a remediation plan - [x] add e2e tests exercising an operator delegation lifecycle across regions - [x] update docs and runbook snippets - [x] telemetry: policy_denied_ttl, auditlink_verify_ok, kms_affinity_mismatch KB/Linear references: ENG-4891 (policy TTL enforcement), SEC-102 (audit-link design), SRE-317 (kms affinity checks). Rollout plan: 1) deploy to staging with feature flags OFF. 2) run migration scanner (tools/bin/scan-stale-bindings) against a snapshot and produce remediation CSV. 3) enable TTL soft-deny mode (record metrics and allow override via operator flag) for two weeks. 4) enable hard deny for tenant groups with low risk. 5) enable HMAC signing and rotate audit verification keys via the key-manager endpoint. 6) enable KMS affinity validator in read-only mode (log+metric only) for 1 week then hard-fail. Backwards compatibility: audit-link signing uses an optional header (X-Audit-Link-Signature). Legacy consumers ignoring the header will continue to receive events. The RBACv2 evaluation path accepts both TTL-marked bindings and legacy bindings; the migration script annotates bindings that require attention. Security considerations: the HMAC secret is stored in KMS-scoped secrets; verification keys are published to the internal key-discovery service with ACLs. The KMS validator only checks location tags and does not change crypto operations. Migration tool: tools/migration/identify_stale_rbac_bindings.py ships in this PR and produces CSV (tenant_id, binding_id, expiry, last_seen, recommended_action). Testing: unit tests for validator logic (policy, auditlink, kms) included; e2e uses a local crypto-proxy test harness and a vm-simulated multi-region runner. Follow-ups: tie TTL metrics to Optimize so customers get suggestions for binding pruning; add a remediation UI in Console; and add an operator CLI to bulk-revoke stale bindings.
